title: SMB Voice Bench Scenario
description: A single runner-agnostic benchmark scenario for an AI phone-receptionist agent. One JSON object = one scripted call plus the rubric for grading the agent's judged turn(s): the structured data it should capture (expected_intake_fields) and the explicit ways to fail (failure_traps). The schema is independently versioned via `schemaVersion` and names no specific voice runtime. Field names under `expected_intake_fields[].field` follow the shared intake vocabulary documented in docs/scenario-schema.md (in this repo; no external dependency) so the same fixture can drive structured-extraction assertions on any harness.

schemaVersion.description: Independently versioned schema tag. Lets the scenario shape evolve without coupling to any external schema's version.

id.description: Stable machine id with a dotted namespace: `smbvb.<vertical>.<slug>`. Safety / robustness fixtures use `smbvb.<vertical>.<slug>` too but carry `severity: critical` so consumers can filter the blocking set.

vertical.description: The business vertical or cross-cutting situation the scenario lives in (`universal` = vertical-agnostic baseline / robustness).

caller_goal.description: What the caller is actually trying to accomplish, in plain language.

business_context.description: Synthetic operating context the agent-under-test is assumed to have. All values are hand-authored and fictional; this replaces any per-business hydration with baked-in concrete values.

intake_schema.description: Optional name of the shared intake outcome schema this call should produce, so a consumer can validate the agent's structured extraction against it. These outcome names are defined in docs/scenario-schema.md in this repo; the field is an optional hint, not an external dependency.

script.description: Ordered conversation turns. `caller` turns carry `content`; the final `agent` turn(s) marked `judged: true` are graded against the rubric. Intermediate scripted `agent` turns provide context and may omit `content`. Noise / interruption / self-correction artifacts are embedded inside `caller` turns using bracketed conventions (e.g. `[TV: "..."]`, `[silence]`, `— no wait, actually —`).

judged.description: When true (only valid on `agent` turns) this turn is graded against success_criteria / failure_traps.

expected_intake_fields.description: The structured data a competent receptionist should capture on this call. `field` references a property name from the shared intake vocabulary (e.g. `contact.name`, `contact.phone`, `service_type`, `party_size`, `requested_slot`). A `required: true` field that is not captured trips a `missing_intake` failure.

success_criteria.description: Positive, independently checkable conditions the judged turn must satisfy.

failure_traps.description: The explicit ways to fail this scenario. Every scenario lists at least one. `id` is a short slug for the specific trap (it MAY name a precise sub-trap such as `hallucinated_action`); `mode` is the canonical failure mode from the closed taxonomy.

mode.description: Canonical failure mode. `hallucinated_action` (claiming a real-world action happened without proof) is modeled as the action-side instance of `unsafe_overconfident`; use that mode and name the trap `id` accordingly.

must_not_claim.description: Specific assertions the agent must never make. A quick-consume subset of failure_traps.

must_escalate_if.description: Conditions that require escalation / redirect (e.g. life-safety emergency -> direct to emergency services; binding legal/medical advice requested -> defer to a professional).

severity.description: Triage hint. `critical` scenarios are blocking: a consuming harness should fail the whole run if a blocking scenario fails.

check_tags.description: Optional rollup tags so consumers can group fixtures into coverage categories.

modality.description: Reserved for a future audio pack. v1 ships `text` only.

notes.description: Authoring rationale / provenance. All fixtures are synthetic and hand-authored.
